answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate and 14-day renewal window force a decision, but the 94% line utilization creates unacceptable risk for sole-source switches. Memory_c2 shows the low-cost vendor has SLA problems on critical lines. Memory_c4 demonstrates that benchmarking pressure on the incumbent recovers real margin without migration risk. Memory_c1 confirms renewal stability. Memory_c6 shows multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing. The optimal move is aggressive renegotiation with the incumbent: benchmark against market rates (c4's proven method), explore volume discounts or multi-year terms (c6's outcome), and secure renewal within the 14-day window. This addresses the cost mandate while preserving the delivery reliability required by line utilization. Verification of c2 (low-cost vendor risk profile) and c4 (negotiation effectiveness) will confirm whether this is the only viable path given the constraint profile. The outcome preserves optionality for future cycles if terms fail to yield sufficient savings.
